description: Audit a project's dependency manifest, configuration and source in one pass: leaked secrets, dangerous patterns and unpinned dependencies, with a risk score and grade. Before shipping or reviewing a project, for a fast consolidated security triage. Do not choose this when you need exploitability confirmed by running the code or a CVE database. Example requests: Audit this project for leaked secrets and dangerous patterns. | Give me a security risk score for this code and config. | Check my dependency manifest for unpinned or URL-sourced packages. | Run a security audit pack over these files.

accepted_price.description: The amount accepted, exactly as quoted (for example "5.00" or 5). Checked against the stored quote, so a price that moved between quote and authorize is refused rather than silently absorbed. Optional, but sent to make the acceptance explicit.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

config.description: The customer's config.env, as text. Supported: Text. The configuration or environment file. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

manifest.description: The customer's manifest.txt, as text. Supported: Text. The dependency manifest (requirements.txt, package.json lines, etc.). Maximum 1048576 bytes.

source.description: The customer's source.py, as text. Supported: Text. The source to scan. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

quote_id.description: The quote_id returned by POST /v1/jobs. Required to authorize a priced capability; the service rejects a priced job that does not name the quote it issued.

name: submit_security_audit_pack

access_token.description: Per-job credential. Present it as the X-Job-Token header to read the job or list it. Keep it; it is the only credential for this job.

verification.description: Independent verification. verification.ok = false means the job failed, not a partial success.

title: Security audit pack
